paragraphs: Every dryer in the all-night laundromat was turning, and behind each round glass door a small warm weather of socks tumbled past. Yellow Duck Sweater stood at the end of the row with six metres of checkered tile ahead of it. On the folding table at the far end sat the giant microduck in a nest of clean laundry, its head sweeping left, then right, like a lighthouse that smelled of soap. The duck crept. Tile, tile, freeze. The floor was cold under its orange feet. Halfway across, one striped sock slipped from the nest and lay on the tiles like a dare.

Each time the giant's head came round, a dryer door swung open and puffed out a cloud of lint to hide in. The duck reached the sock and pushed its head into the cuff to drag it away, and the sock, still warm, slid down over its head and neck like a sleeping bag. The giant looked straight at it. The duck froze, a sock with legs. The giant leaned down, lifted the striped twin from the nest, and set it beside the duck, toe to toe, the way pairs are meant to lie. Under the giant's chin, half buried in towels, a knitted yellow duckling peeked out of a sweater exactly like the duck's own.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The duck stands at the end of a long row of glowing round dryers in an all-night laundromat, with colorful socks tumbling behind every glass door and a checkered tile floor stretching ahead. Panel 2: Two ducks: far across the checkered floor, one giant microduck sits in a nest of clean towels and laundry on a folding table, its huge head turned to one side, while the small duck creeps forward on tiptoe in the foreground. Panel 3: The duck freezes mid-step on the cold checkered tiles, one orange foot raised, staring at a single red-and-white striped sock lying alone on the floor halfway to the nest. Panel 4: A dryer door has swung open beside the duck and a soft grey cloud of lint puffs out around it, half hiding the duck as the giant's head sweeps past in the background. Panel 5: The duck stands on the tiles with a warm red-and-white striped sock pulled down over its whole head and neck like a sleeping bag, its yellow sweater and orange feet sticking out below, frozen still. Panel 6: Two ducks: the giant microduck leans down from its laundry nest and sets a matching red-and-white striped sock on the tiles toe to toe with the sock-covered small duck, and under the giant's chin, half buried in towels, it wears a bright yellow knit sweater with the same cartoon duckling on the front. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
